trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out right or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going around the edge to (1,5) would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going up, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,4); going around the edge to (5,1), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (right from number 1) was wrong, so the line must go left.
Going around the edge to (1,2) would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going up would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes left.
Number 2 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going around the edge to (1,5) would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going left would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up.
Number 3 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Number 4 is only reachable this way.
The line must go down: left is number 10, which comes later.
Going down would leave number 6 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
The line must go left: down is number 8, which comes later.
Going down, the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 8. So the line goes left.
Cell (1,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes around the edge to (1,5).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (2,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going down would force the line onto number 10 before its turn. So the line goes left.
Cell (2,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (3,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
